title: Optional Module B: Photojournalism
summary: With the coming of photography news could be conveyed with greater authority and emphasis; photographs started supporting the written news in newspapers and magazines and photojournalism was born. Early war photographers were the first war photojournalists. Around the 1880s a technology called half tone made it possible to print photographs in newspapers. Photojournalism today is news photography: photographs that support the story of a news event, taken by photojournalists, who often can also write a few words in support of the photograph.

Sports photojournalism (specialised skill and equipment, e.g. cricket); war photojournalism (the earliest form; photographers risking their lives in conflicts and riots); glamour photojournalism (film stars and famous people; such photographers are called paparazzi, an Italian word); spot news photojournalism (day-to-day news such as political events, crime and accidents; the most common and most demanding); travel photojournalism (documentation of an area's landscape, people, cultures, customs and history; amateurs share photographs online through photo-sharing websites); wildlife photojournalism (one of the more challenging forms, needs advanced equipment and knowledge of animal behaviour and terrain). Photojournalists may be employed by a newspaper or freelancers who sell pictures to newspapers and agencies. Scope extends to web-based photojournalism; newspapers and websites also use photos sent by ordinary people with mobile cameras.

A photograph must speak for itself ('a single picture is worth a thousand words'). Composition is the placement of the subject or subjects within the picture frame; it creates impact (a beggar near the camera and a rich man in a big car in the distance shows contrast), makes the picture appealing and energetic (action photographs of war or sports) and demands balance. The rule of thirds is the most common basic rule of framing: elements should fall roughly on the intersections of the lines dividing the frame into three rows and three columns. Camera angle affects composition: a camera below the person's eye level makes the person appear larger (used for leaders and film personalities) and a top angle (above eye level) makes the person look smaller.

A photo feature (photo essay) is a story or essay on a subject told using photographs (a family told in five pictures: meal, father leaving for work, mother cooking, daughter back from school, grandparents watching TV). It is generally conceived at the editor's desk, who briefs the photo editor. A photo editor is the overall in charge of the photo section of a newspaper or magazine; he chooses the photographer, discusses the topic, may choose a reporter to write around the essay, and selects the best pictures that convey the whole story.

vsaB: Name any two types of photojournalism.
Sports photojournalism and war photojournalism (also glamour, spot news, travel, wildlife).
Mention any two advantages of a good composition.
It gives the picture impact and contrast, makes it appealing and balanced, and lets the viewer understand its meaning at once.
Who is a photojournalist? What is meant by wildlife photojournalism?
A photojournalist is a news photographer whose pictures support news stories; wildlife photojournalism photographs animals, needing advanced equipment and knowledge of animal behaviour and terrain.
Briefly discuss the process of bringing out a photo feature in a newspaper or magazine.
The editor conceives it and briefs the photo editor, who chooses the photographer and topic and perhaps a reporter, and selects the best pictures that tell the whole story.
Covering events that make day-to-day news such as political events, crime and accidents; the most common and demanding type.
What is the rule of thirds?
A framing rule that elements should fall near the intersections of lines dividing the frame into three rows and three columns.
laB: Explain the role of photographs in news reporting.

Photographs support written news with authority and emphasis, convey the news at a glance (a single picture is worth a thousand words), enhance the lead story, tell stories through photo essays and use composition for impact.
Briefly discuss the points of consideration of the photo editor for selecting a picture in a newspaper.
The major news events of the day (a picture that enhances the lead story), the hard-hitting nature of the picture that tells a story, and reader interest such as local events.
What is photojournalism? Explain the types with examples.
Photojournalism is news photography supporting stories: sports, war, glamour, spot news, travel and wildlife photojournalism, by employed or freelance photojournalists and now web-based.
